title: Section realization identifies the normalized derived module compositor and identity
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, use the small pro-étale site in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $B_T$ be its reconstructed section-ring sheaf. Write $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$ for the fixed exact equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use the internal module functors $f^*\dashv f_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. On section modules use the ringed-topos morphism whose structural coefficient map is adjunct to $\alpha_f:f^*\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$, or equivalently whose direct-image coefficient map is the reconstructed $\eta_f:\Lambda_Y\to f_*\Lambda_X$. Write $f_{*,s}$ for this sectionwise direct image, and $r_f:E_Yf_*\cong f_{*,s}E_X$ for the comparison of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. For composable arbitrary scheme maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, let $c_{g,f}:g_*f_*\cong(gf)_*$ be [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]; let $c^s_{g,f}$ be the sectionwise geometric compositor, and let $d_T:(1_T)_*\cong1$ and $d^s_T$ be the ordinary identity identifications induced by sectionwise identity maps.

These structural ring maps compose to the structural map for $gf$, including the geometric identification of composite site functors. The comparisons satisfy
$$r_{gf}\circ E_Z(c_{g,f})=(c^s_{g,f}E_X)\circ(g_{*,s}r_f)\circ(r_g f_*),\qquad E_T(d_T)=(d^s_TE_T)\circ r_{1_T}.$$

Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, $D^s_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ and total derived module direct images [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. The termwise equivalence induces $\mathcal E_T=D(E_T)$, preserves and reflects K-injective complexes (a complex $I$ is K-injective when every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic), and identifies resolution transformations. Each $f_*$ preserves K-injective complexes. Write $a_f:\mathcal E_YRf_*\cong Rf_{*,s}\mathcal E_X$ for the canonical resolution-compatible comparison of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization]. Let $\kappa^i_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$ be the total-right-derived comparison induced by $c_{g,f}^{-1}$ and its resolution transformations, and let $\epsilon^i_T:R(1_T)_*\cong1$ be that induced by $d_T$. Let $\kappa^s_{g,f}$ be the independently normalized ringed-topos comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and $\epsilon^s_T$ its identity comparison induced by termwise identity. Put $b_{g,f}=(Rg_{*,s}a_f)\circ(a_gRf_*)$. Then
$$b_{g,f}\circ(\mathcal E_Z\kappa^i_{g,f})=(\kappa^s_{g,f}\mathcal E_X)\circ a_{gf},\qquad \mathcal E_T\epsilon^i_T=(\epsilon^s_T\mathcal E_T)\circ a_{1_T}.$$
For every internal K-injective complex $I$ on $X$, under the canonical resolution identifications, $\kappa^i_{g,f,QI}=[c_{g,f,I}^{-1}]$ and $\epsilon^i_{X,QI}=[d_{X,I}]$. These statements concern the specified transformations and their coefficient actions, include canonical functor associators and equality transports of scheme maps, and impose no properness, finite-type, density, Noetherian or field hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; agent specialization to the internal/sectionwise module equivalence, including the resolution-normalized composition and identity squares.

proof.text: For $V\in Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, the site comparison identifies $(V\times_ZY)\times_YX$ with $V\times_ZX$, with the same projections, as in [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. Apply [lem-sfb-eta-comp]: the coefficient map for $gf$ is $c^{\rm Ab}_{g,f,\Lambda_X}\,g_*^{\rm Ab}(\eta_f)\,\eta_g$. In [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence] take the two base-change site functors, their geometric composite comparison, and coefficient maps $\eta_g,\eta_f$. Its formula for $\phi_\chi$ says exactly that the reconstructed structural ring map for $gf$ is the composite structural ring map, including that site comparison. Thus both ringed-topos compositions in the question use the same coefficient action; no constant-coefficient identification is being substituted.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; coefficient-composition formula in blueprint lem-sfb-eta-comp, and section-ring coherence specialization

proof.text: The comparison $r_f$ of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] is the existing direct-image comparison that is the identity on sections, as recorded in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]; by the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence] it is that lemma's comparison $r_{F,\psi}$ with identity underlying sheaf map. The latter's composition square applies with the coefficient map identified in step 1. Its internal compositor is $c_{g,f}$ of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]: both have the specified geometric underlying sheaf isomorphism, and module morphisms with the same underlying sheaf morphism are equal. Its section compositor is $c^s_{g,f}$ for the same reason. The square therefore reads $r_{gf}E_Z(c_{g,f})=(c^s_{g,f}E_X)(g_{*,s}r_f)(r_gf_*)$. For the identity site functor, [lem-sfb-eta-id] identifies $\eta_{1_T}$ with the inverse geometric identity at $\Lambda_T$, so use the identity clause of the same coherence lemma. The geometric identity identifies $V\times_TT$ with $V$; its restrictions and scalar action are the identity after that identification. This gives $E_T(d_T)=(d^s_TE_T)r_{1_T}$ for the specified ordinary identity maps.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; section-ring composition and identity comparisons

proof.text: By [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization], termwise $E_T$ induces the equivalence $\mathcal E_T$, preserves and reflects K-injectives, transports K-injective resolutions, and gives the specified resolution-compatible $a_f$. K-injective resolutions on section modules exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], since the sites are small in the module universe, and transport across $E_T$ supplies them internally. In particular, if $I$ is K-injective, the source and target of $a_{f,QI}$ identify with $Q(E_Yf_*I)$ and $Q(f_{*,s}E_XI)$, and in these coordinates $a_{f,QI}=Q(r_{f,I})$. This is the resolution-compatibility assertion applied to the identity resolution $I\to I$, not a choice of a new derived comparison.

source.place: Tags 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, and 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; existing section-derived normalization

proof.text: The module adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ is supplied by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] makes this $f^*$ additive exact for every commutative condensed ring and arbitrary scheme map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to conclude that $f_*I$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is. Step 3 also shows that $f_{*,s}E_XI$ is K-injective: it is isomorphic via $r_f$ to $E_Yf_*I$. K-injectivity is invariant under a complex isomorphism, since composing a map and its null-homotopy with that isomorphism transports the defining condition. This does not assert K-injective preservation for an arbitrary ringed-topos direct image with nonexact pullback.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; exactness input: blueprint det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main

proof.text:
Write $\gamma_h:Qh_*\to Rh_*Q$ for the resolution unit. By the universal property in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], the comparison induced by $c^{-1}$ is characterized by
$$\kappa^i_{g,f,QN}\gamma_{gf,N}=Rg_*(\gamma_{f,N})\,\gamma_{g,f_*N}\,Q(c^{-1}_{g,f,N}).$$
Here every factor is typed: $\gamma_{g,f_*N}$ lands in $Rg_*Q(f_*N)$ and then $Rg_*(\gamma_{f,N})$ lands in $Rg_*Rf_*QN$. For K-injective $I$, $\gamma_{gf,I}$, $\gamma_{f,I}$ and $\gamma_{g,f_*I}$ are invertible by step 4 and the K-injective clause of the cited universal property. Removing these resolution identifications leaves exactly $Q(c^{-1}_{g,f,I})$. It also proves invertibility on all objects, since every object has a K-injective representative. Similarly the identity comparison is characterized by $\epsilon^i_{T,QN}\gamma_{1_T,N}=Q(d_{T,N})$, so on $QI$ it is $Q(d_{T,I})$. The arbitrary-resolution and morphism formulas of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] identify all these coordinates with the canonical ones, including resolution transitions; hence these formulas describe the specified transformations.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; resolution-unit universal property and canonical map computation

proof.text: For the independently normalized sectionwise comparison apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the ringed topoi fixed in step 1 and the K-injective complex $E_XI$. By step 4, $f_{*,s}E_XI$ is K-injective, so take its identity map as the intermediate resolution $j$. The cited normalization is then the identity map from $g_{*,s}f_{*,s}E_XI$ to itself after the ordinary composition identification. Before making that identification it is precisely $Q((c^s_{g,f,E_XI})^{-1})$ from $Q((gf)_{*,s}E_XI)$ to $Q(g_{*,s}f_{*,s}E_XI)$. The sectionwise identity comparison induced by termwise identity is likewise $Q(d^s_{T,E_TI})$. Thus the sectionwise normalization has the same orientation as step 5, without identifying two unspecified right-adjoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; stated K-injective normalization with j the identity

proof.text:
Evaluate the desired composition square on $QI$, using steps 3, 5 and 6. The map $a_{g,Rf_*QI}$ is represented by $r_{g,f_*I}$ because $f_*I$ is K-injective. To compute $Rg_{*,s}(a_{f,QI})$, its source $E_Yf_*I$ and target $f_{*,s}E_XI$ are both K-injective; [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] therefore represents it by $g_{*,s}(r_{f,I})$. Consequently the left side is the class of
$$(g_{*,s}r_{f,I})\,r_{g,f_*I}\,E_Z(c^{-1}_{g,f,I}),$$
and the right side is the class of
$$(c^s_{g,f,E_XI})^{-1}\,r_{gf,I}.$$
These are equal: multiply the ordinary square from step 2 on the left by $(c^s)^{-1}$ and on the right by $E_Z(c^{-1})$. All terms are morphisms of modules for the structural ring map already checked in step 1. For identity, steps 3, 5 and 6 reduce the desired square to $Q(E_Td_{T,I})=Q(d^s_{T,E_TI})Q(r_{1_T,I})$, which is exactly the ordinary identity square of step 2.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; agent calculation of the two normalized component formulas

proof.text: The component equalities on K-injectives imply the natural-transformation equalities everywhere. Indeed, for any object $M$ choose a K-injective resolution and the resulting isomorphism $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$. For two natural transformations $t,t':A\Rightarrow B$ in either desired square, naturality gives $t_M=B(u)^{-1}t_{QI}A(u)=B(u)^{-1}t'_{QI}A(u)=t'_M$. The resolution transitions and arbitrary derived morphisms are the canonical ones of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], so this argument is independent of that choice. The site maps and all the displayed compositions retain the geometric comparison from step 1; parentheses are inserted by the ordinary functor associators, and equal scheme maps induce the same restriction maps on sections. Thus the equalities include the stipulated associators and equality transports. Every input used arbitrary scheme maps and commutative condensed coefficients in the stated small universes; no geometric finiteness or field hypothesis has entered.
